Ten stalls have 20 cows each, so the total number of cows is $10 \times 20 = 200$ cows. Mr. Sylas buys 40 cows and divides them equally, so each stall gets $40 \div 20 = 2$ new cows. Therefore, each stall now has $20 + 2 = 22$ cows. 

The question asks how many cows are in 8 of the stalls, so we calculate $8 \times 22 = 176$.

FINAL_ANSWER: 176
